newsitem.title: USA: Household in deal with Transamerica - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Household in deal with Transamerica - WSJ.

text.p: Household International Inc, a consumer-lending and credit card firm, is expected to buy Transamerica Corp's consumer-finance business for more than $1 billion, the Wall Street Journal said.
In Wednesday's electronic edition, the Journal quoted unnamed sources familiar with the deal as saying it was to be announced as early as today.
The acquisition was expected to add to Households' earnings. Transamerica was expected to use the proceeds to repurchase stock, the Journal said.
The acquisition would expand Household's position in consumer financial services, where it already is the No. 2 player in the U.S., the Journal said.
Combined, the two businesses would have about 970 branches in the U.S. and would allow Household to cut costs by combining some operations, the Journal said.
Transamerica's consumer-finance business has about $3.6 billion in assets and 420 branches in 44 states.
